ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a full-wave rectifier circuit with a center-tapped transformer. The primary side on the left is labeled 230 V, 50 Hz, ac; below the transformer it is labeled 230 V/50-0-50 V. The secondary side on the right has a center tap, and the two diodes are labeled D1 and D2 respectively, connected to the load to form a center-tapped full-wave rectifier. Reasoning: Since the primary-side input is the rated 230 V rms, and the secondary side is 50-0-50 V, each half-winding is 50 V rms relative to the center tap. The peak voltage of each half-winding is 50√2 V. In a center-tapped full-wave rectifier, the peak reverse voltage PRV of each diode = 2 × half-winding peak voltage, so PRV = 2 × 50√2 = 100√2 V. The PRV of D1 and D2 is the same.

raw_record.question_text: In the full-wave rectifier shown in the image, the input voltage is 230 V (rms) single-phase AC. What is the peak reverse voltage across diodes \(D_1\) and \(D_2\)?

method.method_draft: Inspect the circuit diagram first and identify a center-tapped full-wave rectifier with a 50-0-50 V secondary. Since the applied primary voltage is the rated 230 V rms, each half-secondary provides 50 V rms with respect to the center tap. Compute one half-secondary peak as 50 sqrt(2) V. Apply the center-tapped full-wave rectifier rule PRV = 2 V_half,peak, giving PRV = 2 × 50 sqrt(2) = 100 sqrt(2) V for both D1 and D2.

method.method_draft: Inspect the image first: D1 is connected to one end of the 50-0-50 V secondary and D2 to the other, with the load returned to the center tap. From the text and transformer label, the primary is operated at its rated 230 V, so each half-secondary is 50 V rms, or 50 sqrt(2) V peak. During the half-cycle when D1 conducts, the output cathode node is at about +50 sqrt(2) V relative to the center tap, while the anode of D2 is at -50 sqrt(2) V. Therefore D2 sees a reverse voltage of +50 sqrt(2) - (-50 sqrt(2)) = 100 sqrt(2) V. By symmetry, D1 has the same PRV on the opposite half-cycle.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Derives the reverse voltage directly from the conducting and nonconducting diode terminal potentials during a half-cycle, without invoking the memorized PRV formula.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read from the image that the transformer secondary has a center tap marked 0, upper and lower ends marked 50 V each side, and that D1 and D2 feed the same output/load node in a center-tap rectifier arrangement.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text to identify that the quantity needed is the peak reverse voltage of D1 and D2 under the stated 230 V rms AC input condition.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: In an ideal rectifier, when one diode conducts, its cathode/output node is clamped approximately to the positive peak of the conducting half-secondary relative to the center tap; simultaneously the opposite secondary end is at the negative peak. The reverse voltage on the off diode is the difference between these two instantaneous potentials.
